issues.legal_issue: Unexplained injuries to an accused do not require rejection of otherwise corroborated prosecution evidence or establish that the accused acted in self-defence.
material_facts: The prosecution witnesses did not explain the injuries found on one accused, whose injuries were recorded soon after the incident.
The injured persons had come to protest the cutting of a tree, and the evidence supported that they were unarmed when the assault began.
Eyewitness testimony identifying the principal assailants was corroborated by medical evidence and the presence of blood at locations along the path of the assault.
The evidence supported that the beating continued as the injured persons tried to flee.
issues.conclusion: The convictions and sentences of the four persons found to have actively assaulted the victims were upheld, and their appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 302/34, 325/34, 323/34 and 147 of the Indian Penal Code, the court assessed the evidence of common participation and the assault. An unexplained injury to an accused is an infirmity that must be considered, but it does not by itself defeat a prosecution account that is supported by credible eyewitness, medical and circumstantial evidence. The evidence did not establish that the victims’ injuries were inflicted in lawful self-defence. No earlier cases were cited.

rule.if: appeal_against_conviction and identified_assailants and credible_eyewitness_account and corroborating_medical_or_scene_evidence and victims_arrived_to_protest and victims_unarmed and accused_sustained_injuries

predicates.appeal_against_conviction: The convicted persons brought an appeal challenging their convictions.
predicates.identified_assailants: Witnesses identified the persons who actively inflicted the assault.
predicates.credible_eyewitness_account: The eyewitness account of the assault was accepted as credible.
predicates.corroborating_medical_or_scene_evidence: Medical findings or physical evidence at the scene supported the eyewitness account.
predicates.victims_arrived_to_protest: The injured persons came to object to an act being carried out by the accused.
predicates.victims_unarmed: The injured persons were not armed when the assault began.
predicates.accused_sustained_injuries: At least one accused had injuries that the prosecution witnesses did not explain.

issues.definition: When a conviction appeal concerns identified assailants, the eyewitness account is corroborated, the victims came unarmed to protest, and an accused’s injuries are also present, the rule states that the conviction and sentence are upheld.

issues.legal_issue: Convictions cannot stand where the evidence against the accused is not safely reliable, lacks independent corroboration, and leaves a reasonable doubt about their participation.
material_facts: The evidence against the four persons attributed only that they surrounded the injured persons and thereby assisted the assault.
The trial court had identified reasons to doubt the independence of the eyewitnesses, and the appellate court did not address all those reasons.
The witnesses did not mention the injuries found on an accused, making it unsafe to rely on their testimony about the four persons without corroboration.
No circumstantial or other reliable evidence independently corroborated the witnesses’ account of those persons’ participation.
Evidence of local factional divisions supported a doubt about whether those persons had been falsely implicated.
issues.conclusion: The convictions of the four persons whose participation was supported only by the unsafe and uncorroborated evidence were set aside, and they were acquitted.
issues.legal_principle: The convictions under Sections 325/149, 323/149 and 147 of the Indian Penal Code required reliable evidence connecting the accused to the unlawful assembly and the assault. Where the witnesses were not fully independent, their account omitted injuries to an accused, and no independent reliable evidence corroborated the alleged participation, it was unsafe to sustain the convictions in the face of a subsisting doubt. No earlier cases were cited.

rule.if: appeal_against_conviction and participation_based_on_witnesses and witnesses_not_fully_independent and witnesses_omitted_accused_injuries and not independent_corroboration_available and factional_doubt_present

predicates.appeal_against_conviction: The convicted persons brought an appeal challenging their convictions.
predicates.participation_based_on_witnesses: The alleged participation of the accused was based on witnesses’ accounts.
predicates.witnesses_not_fully_independent: The evidence disclosed reasons to doubt that the witnesses were fully independent.
predicates.witnesses_omitted_accused_injuries: The witnesses did not mention injuries found on an accused.
predicates.independent_corroboration_available: Reliable circumstantial or other evidence independently supported the account of the accused’s participation.
predicates.factional_doubt_present: Evidence of factional divisions supported a doubt about whether the accused had been falsely implicated.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges convictions based on witness accounts that are not fully independent, omit accused injuries, lack independent corroboration, and are clouded by factional doubt, the rule states that the convictions are set aside and the accused are acquitted.
